claims.short_name: Sharp designated-degree even-D matching deficiency bound
claims.claim_text: For even D≥2 and Δ(G)≤D, a finite simple graph having k vertices of degree exactly D admits a matching leaving at most floor(k/(D+1)) of them uncovered; sharp for disjoint unions of copies of K_(D+1).
claims.support_summary: Complete paper proof via Akiyama-Kano Theorem 1.4.7: each small odd fully-saturated component sends ≥D boundary edges into S, and each large one consumes ≥D+1 saturated vertices; add r universal helper vertices and apply the prescribed matching criterion. Tight disjoint odd-clique examples. General theorem not formally kernel checked.

claims.short_name: Independent finite exact marked-Tutte matching verification
claims.claim_text: An independent exact dynamic-programming matching solver and exhaustive all-S designated odd-component criterion agree for all 685 degree≤4 networkx atlas graphs on ≤7 vertices, 260 seeded larger graphs and disjoint one-to-four K5 examples.
claims.support_summary: Brute vertex-bitmask dynamic programming with matched-vertex reconstruction, independent all-vertex-deletion-set connected-component calculation, exact deficit equality for each graph, and sharpness up to 20 vertices; no built-in maximum-matching solver in this verification path.

claims.short_name: Two universal matching-based avoidance colourings at Δ≤4 and E≤29
claims.claim_text: Every simple graph with maximum degree at most four and at most 29 edges has (A) a red matching and blue at most two degree-four vertices, and (B) a red graph with no three disjoint P3 and a blue graph of maximum degree at most three. Both avoid the designated relevant star pairs; the edge budget 29 is sharp for the corresponding simpler universal target pairs via 3K5.
claims.support_summary: Choose matching missing ≤2 originally degree-four vertices; colour matching red (A), or matching plus every edge incident to unmatched saturated vertices red (B); a red P3 in (B) must meet the two-vertex special set. Independently checked on 685 atlas graphs for both schemes and 330 target-specific exact-edge-count graphs.
